evidence.workload: Short document field extraction into constrained JSON, one request at a time, 32-token output limit, greedy decoding. Minimize memory while retaining 95% of BF16 extraction accuracy and throughput. User wants to fit AI on current hardware. Mixed recipes protect token embeddings, output head, and value/down projections in the first/last eighth of layers and every third middle layer. Other layers use base bits.

prior.source: Completed first search block; no heldout tasks measured in this batch.

pattern_definitions.mlp-and-query-output: MLP gate/up projections use base bits/group_size. Attention q_proj and o_proj use base bits with attention_group_size. All remaining quantizable modules use protected_bits/group_size.
pattern_definitions.all-v-down: All value and down projections plus embedding/head use protected bits; other modules use base bits.
pattern_definitions.all-except-mlp-expansion: Only MLP gate_proj and up_proj use base bits; all other quantizable modules use protected bits.
pattern_definitions.default: Sparse boundary/every-third v/down plus embedding/head protection.

role_plan.reason:
These 15 specialist perspectives form a proposed board. Proposals and the joint ranking are hypotheses derived only from supplied evidence; no separate agents or measurements were run.

Specialist proposals:
1. Weight memory: propose int3-g64 to test lower grouping overhead than int3-g32.
2. Embedding precision: propose vdown4-rest3-g128 to retain explicit 4-bit embedding/head protection.
3. Attention precision: propose mlp-query-output3-ag32 to test 3-bit query/output projections with small attention groups.
4. MLP precision: propose mlp-query-output3-ag32, using the successful mlp3-rest4-g128 trials as supporting evidence for selective MLP compression; their exact pattern is not supplied.
5. Quantization error: propose mixed3-4-g64 to test whether smaller groups repair the quality loss seen with mixed3-4-g128.
6. Group size: propose int3-g64 to probe between int3-g128 quality 0.8 and int3-g32 quality 1.0.
7. Decode latency: propose mlp-query-output3-ag64 as a hypothesis for reducing group overhead during serial decoding.
8. Prefill latency: propose mlp-query-output3-ag64; its prefill effect remains unknown because no phase-specific timings are supplied.
9. Structured extraction: propose mlp-query-output3-ag32 for evaluation on the unchanged constrained-JSON task and 32-token limit.
10. Quality gates: propose mlp-query-output3-ag32 while retaining the 0.95 quality and throughput gates exactly.
11. Measurement noise: propose int3-g64 with the existing identical measurement procedure; interpret throughput against the spread in supplied repeated trials.
12. Search efficiency: propose int3-g64 because it tests an unresolved group-size boundary within the two-candidate budget.
13. Hardware fit: propose int3-g64 and judge actual peak allocated memory; hardware capacity and candidate memory are not supplied.
14. Artifact integrity: propose mlp-query-output3-ag32 with its exact supplied module pattern, bit widths, and group sizes preserved.
15. Failure analysis: propose vdown4-rest3-g128 to test broader value/down protection after sparse protection yielded only 0.85 quality.

Joint proposed ranking, highest priority first:
1. mlp-query-output3-ag32
2. int3-g64
3. mlp-query-output3-ag64
4. mixed3-4-g64
5. vdown4-rest3-g128
6. mixed2-6-g128
7. mixed2-3-g128
8. int2-g128

Measure only the top two. They test selective precision protection and the unresolved 3-bit group-size boundary. The 2-bit recipes rank last because mixed2-4-g128 scored 0.0 quality; that result does not establish their outcomes.

The lowest observed memory among supplied quality-passing recipes is mlp3-rest4-g128 at 2085.734 MiB, with throughput 16.955–17.421. BF16 throughput is absent, so throughput-gate compliance cannot be established from this evidence. No heldout tasks were measured. Final selection must minimize measured peak allocated memory among candidates passing both unchanged gates; the ranking predicts neither qualification nor a memory gain.
